content: `Our [Aug concentration companion](/blog/ai-financing-concentration-2026) answered the distribution question with a multi-lens scoreboard: Amazon ~**41%** of hyperscaler IG, top-3 ~**76%**, HS bloc ~**40%** of the **$489B** AI debt perimeter, HS senior channels ~**49%** of funded stock, QQQ ~**50%** of thematic ETF inflows. The [Q3 financing update](/blog/ai-financing-update-2026q3) then re-printed theme *calendar* weight ??? AI???s share of USD IG from ~**18%** to ~**23%** (+**5** pp) and HY to ~**20%**. This Q3 concentration vintage asks the desk question those two posts imply together: **did the top of the distribution move, or only the theme???s weight inside the calendar?**

The dashboard above is built as a **vintage concentration lens**. Toggle **Aug ??? Q3 deltas**, **Issuer ladder**, **Calendar + stock**, and **Channels + ETF**. The punchline is asymmetric on purpose. **Calendar concentration moved.** Issuer, channel, HS-bloc, and ETF concentration mostly did **not**. Inside the five-name YTD spine (~**$194B**), Amazon is still about **41%** and the top three still clear ~**76%**. Zoom out to the AI debt perimeter and the five names are still a **minority bloc (~40%)**. Zoom into funded credit stock and HS senior unsecured alone is still ~**49%** of ~**$1.065T**. What re-printed is the *share of the primary calendar the theme claims* ??? not who sits at the thick end of the issuer ladder.
## The Q3 scoreboard: sticky tops, moving calendar
| Lens | Aug print | Q3 print | Delta | What it measures |
| Hyperscaler IG top-1 (Amazon) | **~41%** | **~41%** | **0 pp** | Five-name ~$194B universe |
| Hyperscaler IG top-3 | **~76%** | **~76%** | **0 pp** | AMZN ?? GOOGL ?? META |
| HS bloc of AI debt perimeter | **~40%** | **~40%** | **0 pp** | Share of ~$489B AI-related debt |
| Funded channel top-1 (HS senior) | **~49%** | **~49%** | **0 pp** | Booth/Hepp ~$1.065T funded stock |
| AI share of USD IG supply | **~18%** | **~23%** | **+5 pp** | Theme weight in IG calendar |
| AI share of US HY supply | **~18%** | **~20%** | **+2 pp** | Theme weight in HY calendar |
| AI-tagged share of US IG stock | ??? | **~15%** | Q3 lens | Outstanding stock, not flow |
| Big-5 path in major IG indices | ??? | **~5%** | Q3 path | YE2026 index-weight path |

Read the table as a **family of market shares with a vintage tag**, not one concentration number. The issuer ladder inside the hyperscaler cohort remains thick. Theme-stack concentration remains milder once utilities, DC JVs, and ecosystem credit enter the perimeter. Channel-stock concentration remains extreme at the senior sleeve. What Q3 adds is evidence that **calendar absorption can concentrate even while issuer ranks stay sticky** ??? the theme claims more of the tape without Amazon needing a larger *inside* share of the five-name spine.
## Aug ??? Q3 deltas: which meters moved

Open **Aug ??? Q3 deltas**. Filter to **Moved only** and the chart collapses to two bars: USD IG and US HY theme shares. Filter to **Sticky only** and the issuer top-1 / top-3, HS bloc, and channel top-1 prints sit flat. That is the analytical hinge for this vintage. Desks that underwrite ???concentration rose in Q3??? without specifying *which meter* will confuse a calendar re-print with an issuer re-ladder. Desks that underwrite ???nothing changed because Amazon is still ~41%??? will miss that the same sticky ladder now sits inside a theme that claims roughly a **quarter** of USD IG gross supply.

The companion calendar panel makes the delta visual: Aug **18% / 18%** (IG / HY) versus Q3 **23% / 20%**. The cross-lens scatter then places the IG-calendar lens apart from sticky issuer, channel, and ETF points ??? high on the ???theme top-1??? axis but without a meaningful top-3 issuer ladder because it is a *theme share*, not a ranked cohort.

Pair this view with the [mid-year $489B update](/blog/ai-financing-update-2026) if you need the perimeter definition, and with the [Aug concentration companion](/blog/ai-financing-concentration-2026) if you need the full multi-lens scoreboard without the vintage filter.
## Issuer ladder: still Amazon, still three-quarters at top-3

Switch to **Issuer ladder**. The cumulative curve for the five-name YTD universe still rises to about **41%** at top-1, **61%** at top-2, and **76%** at top-3. Approximate HHI on five buckets sits near **2,470** ??? well above an equal five-way split (~2,000). Amazon???s disclosed multi-tranche USD/EUR prints remain the modal top-1; Alphabet and Meta fill the next rungs; Oracle???s releveraging path and Microsoft???s still-OCF-heavy posture close the ladder.

That is concentrated relative to five equal issuers. It is **not** a single-name monopoly, and Q3 did not make it more monopolistic on the carried deal tape. A system where three names clear three-quarters of hyperscaler IG still leaves Oracle and Microsoft as material supply ??? and still leaves the entire five-name bloc as only **40%** of the broader AI debt tape. The Q3 contribution is to show that this *inside* distribution can stay sticky while the *outside* calendar weight of the theme climbs.

Debt is still only about a **third** of hyperscaler capex on Goldman???s path (carried from the [research spine](/blog/ai-financing-research-2026)). Concentration of *issuance* can coexist with concentration of *cash-flow funding* ??? Amazon can dominate the bond calendar while the cohort as a whole still funds the majority of servers from operating cash flow.
## Calendar + stock: theme weight and outstanding claims

Open **Calendar + stock**. The dual-line path shows AI???s share of US IG gross supply climbing from ~**1%** in 2024 to ~**7%** in 2025, ~**18%** at the August desk print, and ~**23%** in the Q3 refresh ??? with HY near **20%**. Toggle **HY line** off if you want the IG-only spine. Theme weight inside the calendar can concentrate without any single issuer matching Amazon???s inside-cohort share.

## Calendar + stock: theme weight and outstanding claims

Open **Calendar + stock**. The dual-line path shows AI???s share of US IG gross supply climbing from ~**1%** in 2024 to ~**7%** in 2025, ~**18%** at the August desk print, and ~**23%** in the Q3 refresh ??? with HY near **20%**. Toggle **HY line** off if you want the IG-only spine. Theme weight inside the calendar can concentrate without any single issuer matching Amazon???s inside-cohort share.

The stock-and-index panel adds the Q3 lenses the Aug concentration post did not meter as tightly: AI-tagged paper near **~15%** of US IG *stock*, Big-5 path weight near **~5%** of major IG indices by YE2026, the sticky HS bloc at **40%** of the AI debt perimeter, and private data-centre transactions near **~$200B** since early 2025 overlapping the private-credit sleeve (~**19%** of funded stock). Flow concentration and stock concentration are related but not identical. A market can look diversified on monthly deal tapes while outstanding claims and index weights slowly thicken around the same names.

Treat the **15% / 5%** prints as **stock and path meters**, not stress-loss forecasts. JPM-style absorption maps (~**$300B** next-year absorb against a multi-year funding need near **~$1.5T**) sit in the [Q3 financing update](/blog/ai-financing-update-2026q3); this lens only borrows the concentration-relevant slices.

## Channels + ETF: senior sleeve and Mag-7 proxy flows

Toggle **Channels + ETF**. The Booth/Hepp stock map carried in our [August 202608 update](/blog/ai-financing-update-202608) still puts funded AI-infra credit near **$1.065T**. HS senior unsecured alone is about **$520B / 49%**. Project / data-centre finance (~**$250B / 23%**) and private credit (~**$200B / 19%**) push the **top-3 channel share to ~91%**. ABS and GPU-secured sleeves remain thin residuals. Q3???s quantified private-DC deal tally (~**$200B**) does not overturn that ranking ??? it *explains* why the private-credit rung is already a fifth of the funded map.

On the equity side, FactSet???s 2025 US thematic ETF inflow sleeve remains about **$43.5B**, with **QQQ alone absorbing ~$21.7B ??? roughly 50%**. Semiconductor proxies add another ~**20%**; narrow robotics/AI thematics remain a thin wedge. Equity-side concentration is still a **sentiment-capacity** meter. Creations into QQQ are not issuer proceeds for Amazon???s data centres; they are secondary ownership of a Mag 7???heavy Nasdaq-100 proxy. The Q3 financing story does not re-ladder that sleeve ??? it reminds desks that public-market *ownership* concentration and credit *issuance* concentration can both be top-heavy without being the same object.

## Who is exposed ??? and what would change the story

**Exposed:** IG portfolios that treat ???hyperscaler??? as five equal credits when three names still clear ~**76%** of YTD issuance *and* the theme now claims ~**23%** of USD IG supply; desks that read the Q3 calendar jump as proof the issuer ladder flattened (it did not); insurers and pensions whose AI-infra exposure is mostly the **$520B** senior sleeve and therefore inherit issuer-ladder concentration whether or not they own project-finance paper; equity allocators who read thematic ETF creations as diversified AI exposure when half the sleeve is QQQ; index-sensitive IG mandates that will feel Big-5 path weight near **~5%** even if they never buy a ???AI bond??? sleeve by name.

**Relative winners under current rules:** mega-issuers that can still clear multi-tranche books inside AA/A technicals while the calendar saturates around the theme; intermediaries that intermediate overflow into project finance and private credit as IG calendars absorb more AI supply; holders of the senior unsecured sleeve while lease overhang and GPU-secured risk sit elsewhere in the capital stack; broad-proxy ETF complexes that capture Mag 7 ownership demand without needing narrow AI wrappers.

**What would change the story:** a sustained flattening of the issuer ladder so top-1 falls below ~**25%** of hyperscaler IG *while* calendar weight stays elevated; ecosystem debt growing so fast that the HS bloc share of the AI perimeter falls well below **30%** *and* issuer concentration inside the bloc breaks; a funded-stock mix where project + private credit displace HS senior below ~**35%**; thematic ETF flows dispersing so no single ticker holds more than ~**30%** of the sleeve; a Q4 calendar re-print that *reverses* the +5 pp IG jump without a matching issuer re-ladder. None of those appear in the mid-2025 to Q3-2026 vintages summarised here.

## Caveats and methodology

- **Issuer shares inside the five-name YTD spine are estimated** from disclosed Reuters/LSEG deal prints and close to the Goldman ~**$194B** total. Q3 carries the Aug concentration ladder as **sticky** ??? treat top-1 / top-3 as order-of-magnitude concentration, not a prospectus table.
- **AI debt perimeter (~$489B) mixes IG, HY, loans, and ecosystem credit**; the **40%** HS share is a bloc share, not an issuer ladder.
- **IG/HY calendar weights (~23% / ~20%)** are theme shares of gross supply ??? not top-1 issuer shares of the calendar. The +5 / +2 pp deltas are desk re-prints versus the Aug mid-year update.
- **Channel stock (~$1.065T)** is a research synthesis (Booth/Hepp map); private-credit and some project sleeves are estimated and can overlap the Q3 ~**$200B** DC deal tallies.
- **AI-tagged IG stock (~15%)** and **Big-5 index path (~5%)** are Q3 stock/path lenses, not flow issuer shares.
- **Uncommenced leases (~$675B)** remain excluded from funded-stock concentration by design.
- **ETF flows are net creations, not AUM**, and QQQ is a Mag 7 proxy rather than a pure AI product.
- **Equity raises** (e.g. Alphabet???s mid-2026 ~**$85B** print) are excluded from the IG issuer ladder on purpose ??? they concentrate *funding* without concentrating *bond* supply.

## The shareable takeaway

AI financing in Q3 is **concentrated at the top ??? and the top that moved is the calendar, not the issuer ladder**. Theme weight inside USD IG re-printed at ~**23%** (+**5** pp versus Aug) and HY at ~**20%**. Inside hyperscaler IG, top-1 (Amazon) is still about **41%** and top-3 about **76%**. Of the **$489B** AI debt perimeter, the five-name bloc is still only ~**40%**. Of funded credit stock, HS senior unsecured alone is still ~**49%** and the top-3 channels clear ~**91%**. Of thematic ETF inflows, QQQ still takes ~**50%**. The build-out is funded in credit and public markets through a system that looks more *theme-heavy in the primary calendar* without looking less *issuer-heavy inside the five-name spine*.

| Wafer-fab equipment (WFE) | **~22%** (Applied) | **~56%** | **~1,120** | Upstream |

Read the table as a **family of market shares**, not one semiconductor ???concentration number.??? A system where EUV is a monopoly, leading-edge logic is a near-monopoly, HBM is a tight oligopoly, and broad WFE is a diversified oligopoly will produce wildly different risk narratives depending on which layer you quote. Analysts who cite only TSMC???s overall foundry share (~**62%**) understate how sharp concentration becomes at the AI-relevant node; analysts who cite only ASML understate that packaging and HBM still gate the ship even when lithography tools exist.

## Layer ladder: where top-1 saturates before top-3

Open **Layer ladder**. The horizontal bars rank eight stack layers by top-1, top-3, or approximate HHI. Toggle **Stage** to isolate upstream tools, midstream manufacturing, or downstream accelerators. The companion **top-k path** chart shows how fast cumulative share saturates: EUV, foundry, and GPUs are already near ceiling at top-1; HBM and CoWoS still climb meaningfully into top-2/top-3; WFE never saturates ??? its top-3 stays near **56%**.

That ordering is the concentration post???s contribution relative to a simple bottleneck score. Tightness and share are related but not identical. CoWoS prints the highest editorial tightness (**10**) with top-1 ~**78%**; EUV prints tightness **9** with top-1 **100%**. HBM sits at tightness **9** with a ???only??? **53%** top-1 ??? because the *market* is three players, not one, yet every AI GPU still needs HBM from that closed set.

The Lorenz-style panel under the top-k path accumulates top-1 mass across layers ranked by concentration. It sits well above an equal-share guide: the first few layers already carry most of the ???single-vendor risk??? mass in the stack.

## Foundry versus HBM: two midstream shapes

Switch to **Foundry / HBM**. The dual bars contrast **advanced-node** share with **overall foundry** share. TSMC???s ~**90%** leading-edge print versus ~**62%** overall is the cleanest demonstration that AI-relevant concentration is sharper than the mature-node census. Samsung and Intel Foundry remain in the advanced race but do not dilute TSMC???s tip-of-the-distribution dominance on the nodes that ship frontier GPUs.

The HBM donut and cumulative ladder tell a different midstream story. SK Hynix ~**53%**, Samsung ~**35%**, Micron ~**12%** ??? top-3 equals the market. There is no long tail. That is why HBM binds schedules even without a 90% top-1: when three vendors are the entire supply set and qualification cycles are long, buyer diversification is limited by physics and contracts, not by a missing fourth supplier on a slide.

For the packaging gate that sits beside HBM, see the theme???s [GPU packaging & memory bottleneck](/blog/ai-gpu-packaging-memory-bottleneck-2025) frame and the [Q3 CoWoS tracker](/blog/ai-supply-chain-update-2026q3): capacity can rise toward **~140k wpm** while the supply-demand gap reprints near **20%** when demand re-accelerates and NVIDIA reservations lock **more than half** of the pool.

## Share ?? tightness: single points of failure

Open **Share ?? tightness**. The scatter plots each layer???s top-1 share against an editorial bottleneck score (1???10), with bubble size scaled to approximate HHI. The upper-right cluster ??? EUV, leading-edge foundry, CoWoS, AI GPUs ??? is where concentration and scarcity reinforce each other. WFE and wafers sit lower-left on share even when tools are expensive: broader equipment markets still have multiple credible vendors.

The stage-colored bars beside the scatter answer *where* concentration lives in the chain. Upstream is bifurcated: EUV is absolute monopoly; EDA is a strong duopoly/triopoly; broad WFE is comparatively flat. Midstream is where AI manufacturing risk concentrates ??? foundry, HBM, CoWoS. Downstream AI GPUs inherit that structure and add their own ~**88%** NVIDIA print.

## Regions and CoWoS: geography plus buyer concentration

Open **Regions / CoWoS**. SEMI???s 2025 WWSEMS billings still put **China + Taiwan + Korea at ~79%** of global equipment dollars ??? a geographic top-3 that rivals vendor concentration inside several layers. China alone is ~**36.5%** of billings; Taiwan???s near-doubling into 2025 remains the AI-install signature the [research post](/blog/ai-supply-chain-research-2026) emphasized.

The CoWoS composed panel tracks capacity (wpm) against **NVIDIA reservation share** and the supply gap across research ??? Aug mid ??? Q3 ??? Mid-Year vintages. Capacity rises; the buyer share at the tip of the packaging queue stays near **~55%**. That is concentration on the *demand* side of a midstream bottleneck ??? complementary to TSMC???s supply-side share of CoWoS-class capacity.

## Why WFE looks ???diversified??? next to EUV

The most common analytical error in this theme is collapsing ???semiconductor equipment??? into one concentration statement. ASML???s EUV monopoly is real. Applied Materials / ASML / Lam as a ~**56%** top-3 in broad WFE is also real. Quoting either without the other mis-states resilience. Export controls, tool lead times, and service networks still create friction in diversified WFE ??? but the industrial-organisation object is different from a single-scanner monopoly.

EDA sits between those poles: Synopsys + Cadence already clear roughly **~72%**, and top-3 approaches **~88%**. Design-software concentration rarely makes shipping headlines the way CoWoS does, yet it shapes who can implement advanced nodes at all.

## Caveats

- **Layer shares are public narrative bands and company-disclosure composites**, not a single SEMI census of vendor revenue by AI-relevant slice. Treat advanced-foundry and GPU percentages as order-of-magnitude structure, not filing-precision microdata.
- **HHI figures are derived** from stated top buckets plus a residual; they are analytical meters for ranking layers, not antitrust exhibits.
- **Tightness scores are editorial** (1???10) carried from the theme???s bottleneck framework; they are not SEMI metrics.
- **CoWoS ???share??? mixes capacity ownership and buyer reservation narratives** across vintages ??? useful for concentration storytelling, not a substitute for TSMC???s full packaging P&L.
- **Regional equipment shares** are install geography (where tools ship), not where corporate parents are headquartered.

## What to watch next

Watch whether leading-edge foundry top-1 softens as Intel Foundry and Samsung qualify more AI silicon ??? or whether TSMC???s advanced share stays near **90%** even as overall foundry share holds the low-60s. Watch HBM: a true fourth supplier would change the oligopoly math; incremental Micron share inside a three-player set would not. Watch CoWoS and rival advanced-packaging ramps: capacity growth without buyer diversification still leaves NVIDIA reservation share as a demand-side concentration print. And keep EUV as the upstream ceiling ??? High-NA does not create a second EUV vendor.
